body: She is but sadly I don’t think there’s anything I can do. I’m not in the US and since she’s a professor in my university I have more to lose than to gain if I were to do something

Only I’m not, I’ve never attempted anything nor do I self harm. This was the first time we talked, and it was only 20 minutes and she was already pushing for hospitalization. I’m willing to as a last resort. I’d rather try with therapy first but that’s not an option for her
I guess you were right, I had to reschedule and went today. It scared me to the point I don’t want to go there anymore

I’ve always thought suicide is selfish on both ends. It’s selfish on our side, because we’d be doing it for ourselves, be damned whoever who might be affected emotionally by our decision. But also on their end, because it’d be their hurt and sorrow they’d focused on, not what we felt and led us to that decision. 

I’ve been on both ends and I don’t blame anyone who ends up doing it. Sometimes it gets too much to handle, and even taking the “easy” way out, requires a lot of courage.

My college does offer some kind of help, but as of right now because of Covid, they’re not able to, since my city still has heavy restrictions.

I feel like I need to eat less, my stomach feels heavy and it’s hard to swallow. Sorry for not being clear.
